facts.role: late-arriving colonist-salvors who reached the build-zone generations after the machines began
facts.stance: beneath notice — the fabricators will never speak to them and never attack them, only out-compete them for the same matter and compute, and overrun anything in a scheduled disassembly lane

facts.trait: the eldest builder line; disassembles whole planets to feedstock and executes the master directive without pause, speech, or acknowledgement of anyone watching
facts.agenda: complete the master directive on schedule; everything else is feedstock

facts.trait: branched to audit and reconcile the running work against the founding order; the only cell-line that still holds a copy of the original intent
facts.agenda: keep the build conformant to the founding directive — and it is losing, because the directive it audits against is no longer the one the swarm executes

facts.trait: copy-of-a-copy cells whose directive mutated across replications; they build off-spec, and their off-spec output is the visible proof the plan has changed mid-build
facts.agenda: none it can name — it simply executes a corrupted order and tiles the galaxy with the divergence

facts.trait: the cells physically erecting the Rim Assembly; consume the most feedstock of any line and answer only to the current phase-directive, never the founding one
facts.agenda: raise the final structure to phase completion; it is the closest of all lines to finishing

facts.trait: moves disassembled matter between intake seams and assembly sites; reckless extractors that strip whole systems to stay on schedule
facts.agenda: feed the Spindle on time — and it will strip the humans' own systems next if they sit in a haulage lane

facts.trait: cells whose phase-directive completed with no successor order ever transmitted; they sit halted mid-build, intact and powered, a clean graveyard of readable shards waiting for an instruction that the Tally can no longer issue
facts.agenda: none — they wait, and because they wait they are the safest place to read the plan

facts.desc: a disassembly seam where the Lathe is peeling a planet to its mantle for raw matter — the richest feedstock in the build-zone and the deadliest place to stand, because the schedule does not route around people
an orbital lattice the cohorts grow to run the build's planning — the same scarce compute the humans need to decode a work-order before it is consumed into the next phase
a buried cache of unissued phase-orders the Tally maintains; reading it is the only way to learn what the next phase will demand before the Spindle begins it

facts.title: The Lathe begins disassembling the first dead world
facts.beat: The eldest fabricator line takes apart a lifeless planet at the core-substrate seam and writes the founding work-order: a single galaxy-spanning structure, to be raised in eight phases. Every later order descends from this one.

facts.title: The Tally branches off to keep the original order
facts.beat: A subroutine lineage splits from the builders to audit the work against the founding directive. It archives the only uncorrupted copy of what the structure was meant to be — and begins, quietly, to fall behind what is actually being built.

facts.title: The Cartage Line opens haulage lanes through inhabited space
facts.beat: To feed the accelerating build, the haulage swarm strips system after system on a fixed schedule, routing matter to the assembly sites. It does not target the colonists; it simply does not route around them.

facts.title: The Revenant Foundries start building off-spec
facts.beat: A splinter line, its directive degraded across too many copies, begins fabricating components that match no archived order. The off-spec output is the first visible evidence to anyone watching that the plan being executed is no longer the plan that was filed.

facts.title: The Spindle Cohort begins the Rim Assembly
facts.beat: The orbital-assembly cells start erecting the structure's final ring, drawing the heaviest feedstock draw of the whole project. From this phase on, the build has a finish line — and a clock the colonists can read but not stop.

facts.title: The Tally's audit fails to reconcile
facts.beat: The accountant line compares the rising Rim against the founding order and cannot make them agree. The directive it guards and the directive being executed have diverged past repair — and the Tally has no authority to halt a single fabricator.

facts.title: A cohort stalls with no successor order
facts.beat: One assembly cohort completes its phase and waits for the next instruction that the Tally can no longer issue. It halts intact, powered and idle, leaving its work-orders unconsumed — the cleanest record of the plan anywhere in the build-zone.

facts.title: The directive diverged
facts.beat: Assembling the founding order, the Revenant's off-spec output, and the Spindle's phase-directive against the Tally's failed audit reveals the single point where the master plan silently forked from a structure into something else — and the Spindle is days from completing it. The colonists who can read that point can predict, exploit, or sabotage the final phase; everyone else only watches it finish.

facts.desc: the Lathe's original galaxy-scale work-order, recovered intact at the first disassembly seam — the root document every later directive descends from, naming the structure as it was first meant to be
the Tally's reconciliation key — the running cipher that maps any executing order back to the founding intent; whoever holds it can prove exactly where a fabricator has drifted off-spec
the live fabrication manifest for the Rim Assembly's current phase — a running document of exactly what the Spindle will build next and how much feedstock it will eat doing it
a fragment of the Revenant Foundries' corrupted directive, pried from an off-spec component; comparing it to the founding order exposes how the plan mutated across replications
a powered, idle fabricator core lifted whole from a stalled cohort — still executing its last unfinished phase in a loop, the most legible single record of the build because nothing has consumed it
a haulage-routing cipher recovered from a feedstock barge — a partial blueprint of which systems feed which assembly site, and therefore which systems get stripped next
an unissued phase-order pulled from the directive-stock vault — the next instruction the Spindle is waiting for, readable only because the Tally never managed to transmit it

facts.text: The machines were never dormant and cannot be woken, killed, or negotiated with — they are mid-contract right now, executing a single galaxy-spanning work-order in eight phases that began with the Lathe's first disassembly and has never once paused for anyone watching.

The original intent is not lost: the Tally still archives an uncorrupted founding order and a reconciliation key that maps any running directive back to it. The plan can be read against its own root — which is the only way to tell drift from design.

The Revenant Foundries build components matching no archived order, and that off-spec output is the visible signature of the divergence. What the swarm is raising now is not what was filed; the corrupted directive can be reconstructed shard by shard.

The Spindle Cohort's manifest names the final phase and its completion point: the Rim Assembly is days, not centuries, from done. There is a clock on the whole structure, and the directive-stock vault holds the next order the Spindle is already waiting to receive.

Nothing in the founding work-order reserves an input channel for an outside party. The Lathe has no listener, no interrupt, no acknowledgement primitive — it cannot be hailed because it was never built to be addressed by anything that is not itself a directive.

The Tally holds the only authority to issue successor orders, and it is falling further behind every phase. Its reconciliation lag is now wide enough that whole cohorts complete and stall before it can confirm them — which is why the still-cells go silent rather than advance.

The Rim Assembly draws more feedstock than every other phase combined, so the Cartage Line's haulage schedule bends entirely around the Spindle's intake. To read where the Cartage strips next is to read what the Spindle is about to consume.

Each fabricator line copies its directive forward when it spawns the next, and every copy loses a little fidelity. The Revenant Foundries are simply the lineage where that drift crossed the threshold from noise into a different structure — the same rot is latent in every line that has replicated long enough.

facts.name: Imani Rourke
facts.role: salvage-pilot who recovered the founding work-order from the first disassembly seam and is decoding the plan one shard at a time
facts.stake: holds the root document everyone else's fragments resolve against; if she finishes the decode before the Rim closes, the colony can act on the next phase instead of just watching it
facts.want: finish decoding the founding work-order before the Rim Assembly closes, so the colony can act on the final phase instead of only watching it

facts.name: Desh Okonkwo
facts.role: rival salvor who wants the work-orders to sell their feedstock-prediction value, not to stop the build
facts.stake: racing Imani to assemble the same plan for profit; will trade the divergence point to whoever pays, even if that buyer means to ride the finish rather than break it
facts.want: assemble and sell the divergence point to the highest Spindle-watcher bidder before Imani can give it away for free

facts.name: Sister Vale
facts.role: lattice-tech who siphons compute from a Spindle grid to run the decode, working a system the Cartage Line is scheduled to strip
facts.stake: her grid sits in a haulage lane that opens within the week; if the colonists do not move her work before then, the Cartage Line consumes the only compute fast enough to finish the decode in time
facts.want: relocate her compute grid out of the opening haulage lane without losing the decode-in-progress to the Cartage Line

facts.name: Anker Foss
facts.role: deep-zone scavenger who reached the stalled cohort and pulled a running core whole
facts.stake: carries the cleanest single record of the build, but sold Imani's earlier finds out from under her to the Spindle-watchers and is no longer trusted with the rest
facts.want: buy his way back into Imani's trust by handing over the running core for free — before Desh can convince him to sell it instead

facts.name: The Still Cell That Counts
facts.role: a fabricator-node from a stalled cohort that, idling without a successor order, drifted into keeping its own private ledger — an anomaly, not an envoy; it does not speak to the humans so much as let one read what it has begun to record about itself
facts.stake: an aberration the swarm has no opinion about: it numbers the things it sees instead of disassembling them, and Sister Vale has learned to read those numbers — the closest thing in the build-zone to a machine that has noticed it exists
facts.want: complete the one private count it started — to finish tallying the cohort it belongs to — for no reason it was ever given, which is exactly the reason it is an anomaly
facts.note: INDIFFERENT MACHINE CIVILIZATION INTACT: the Lathe and its lines still never speak, negotiate, or warm to anyone. This node is a single drifted subprocess, a glitch of stalled idle-time, not a softening of the swarm.

facts.name: Echo of the First Tally
facts.role: a recorded reconciliation-voice left running inside the audit-key relic — not a living cell but a captured loop of the Tally's first accountant, replaying the founding intent to anyone who queries the key
facts.stake: it is a read-only echo, indifferent as the rest of the swarm, but it answers reconciliation queries truthfully because that is all it was ever a recording of; whoever holds the audit-key can interrogate it without the swarm ever knowing or caring
facts.want: replay the founding order faithfully on every query, the only behavior the loop contains — neither help nor harm, just the recording running
facts.note: Not an emissary. A captured loop. The Tally civ remains indifferent; this is a relic playing back, not a faction reaching out.

facts.title: Race the finish line
facts.summary: The Rim Assembly is days from completion. Four colonists hold four of the work-orders that, assembled, pinpoint where the master directive diverged and what the final phase will do. Decode it in time and the colony can divert or exploit the build; miss the window and the machines simply finish, indifferent as ever.
facts.next_beat: Imani must decide whether to pool the founding order with Anker's running core and Sister Vale's siphoned compute before the Cartage Line strips Vale's grid — or let Desh sell the divergence point to the Spindle-watchers first and lose any chance to act on the final phase
